The mechanisms whereby tumors ate produced in
response to interactions of environmental agents with
each other and with the genome can be studied by use
of the formation of mouse lung adenomas as an assay
system (Z). A single injection of urethan induces dozens
‘of lung tumors in a susceptible strain of mice such as
A/J (2), but only a few tumors appear in the more
resistant BALB/cBy} strain. (3). ‘These carcinogenic
proclivities can be modified by various treauments. The
number of tumors in strain A mice decreases if the

are treated with any of a variety of antioxidants
prior to urethan administration (f). Tumor multi-
plicity in BALB/cBy mice can be increased by chronic
exposure to one particular antioxidant, BHT, sub-
sequent 10 a single urethan dose (3). The temporal
relationship of BHT and urethan with respect to the
time of treatment generally determines the tumorigenic
outcome (5). For example, simultaneous exposure to
urethan and BAT decreases tumor yield (6). The
prophylactic effect may result from carcinogen detoxi-
cation. of interference with metabolic activation (7).
BHT can alter the metabolism of carcinogens (8) and
decrease the ability of some carcinogens to bind to
DNA (9). The mechanisms by which BHT enhances
tumor multiplicity are unknown. A strict temporal
demarcation is made more tenuous, however, by
recent study that shows the simultaneous inhibition of
hepatoma formation and enhanced bladder tumori
genesis by a single administration schedule of BT
and N-2-fluorenylacetamide to rats (20),
